items.informal_name: Sum over Finite Set Bounded by Cardinality Times Maximum Element
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {N : Type u_5} [inst : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_1 : PartialOrder N] [AddLeftMono N] (s : Finset ι)
  (f : ι → N) (n : N), (∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ n) → s.sum f ≤ s.card • n
items.informal_description: For any additive commutative monoid $N$ equipped with a partial order $\leq$ where addition is left-monotonic, given a finite set $s$, a function $f : \iota \to N$, and an element $n \in N$, if $f(x) \leq n$ for all $x \in s$, then the sum of $f(x)$ over all $x \in s$ is less than or equal to the product of the cardinality of $s$ and $n$. Symbolically, $\sum_{x \in s} f(x) \leq |s| \cdot n$.

items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {N : Type u_5} [inst : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_1 : PartialOrder N] [AddLeftMono N] (s : Finset ι)
  (f : ι → N) (n : N), (∀ x ∈ s, n ≤ f x) → s.card • n ≤ s.sum f
items.informal_description: For any finite set $s$ of type $\iota$ and function $f : \iota \to N$ where $N$ is an additive commutative monoid equipped with a partial order and left addition monotonicity, if every element $x \in s$ satisfies $n \leq f(x)$, then the scalar multiplication of the cardinality of $s$ by $n$ is less than or equal to the sum of $f$ over $s$. Formally, $|s| \cdot n \leq \sum_{x \in s} f(x)$.

items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_3} [inst : AddMonoid M] [inst_1 : Preorder M] [AddRightMono M] [AddLeftMono M] (l : List M) (n : M),
  (∀ (x : M), x ∈ l → x ≤ n) → l.sum ≤ l.length • n
items.informal_description: In an additive monoid equipped with a preorder where addition is monotonic on both sides, for any list $ l $ of elements and any element $ n $, if every element $ x $ in $ l $ satisfies $ x \leq n $, then the sum of the list $ \sum l $ is less than or equal to the product of the list's length and $ n $, i.e., $ \sum l \leq \mathrm{length}(l) \cdot n $. Here, $ \cdot $ denotes the canonical scalar multiplication by natural numbers in the additive monoid.

items.informal_description: In an additive monoid $M$ equipped with a preorder where addition is monotonic on both sides, if every element $x$ in a list $l$ satisfies $n \leq x$, then the scalar multiplication of $n$ by the length of $l$ is less than or equal to the sum of the list elements. Formally, if $\forall x \in l, n \leq x$, then $\text{length}(l) \cdot n \leq \sum_{x \in l} x$.
